intro: Here in Adana province, the Adana Museum moved in 2017 into the halls of a textile mill founded at the start of the twentieth century — one of the largest museum buildings in Türkiye. Under its roof are gathered the Hittite and Roman finds of the Çukurova plain.
history: In 2017 the museum moved into the restored halls of the Milli Mensucat textile mill, built at the start of the twentieth century, and became one of the largest museum buildings in Türkiye. Alongside finds that run from the mounds of the Çukurova to its Roman cities, it also displays something unexpected: the mill's own looms.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the mill halls themselves, the Hittite and Neo-Hittite works, the Roman sarcophagi and, of course, the looms.
facts: Did you know? Part of the museum is arranged as industrial heritage, so a Roman sarcophagus and a weaving loom stand under the same roof. The museum moved into the halls of a textile mill from the start of the twentieth century, becoming one of the largest museum buildings in Türkiye. And the mill's looms were left where they stood, which is why Roman sarcophagi and industrial heritage are shown side by side.
outro: This brings our journey through the Adana Museum to an end. Please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash. Ancient stone and old machinery alike deserve our care. Enjoy your visit.
